scope: Owner-authorized S2 delta and proposed repair packets, nonpromoting

findings.detail: The F6 HTTP sensor ('R17 discovery read-role denial finishes before actual global source writer release') cannot tell the corrected code from the uncorrected code. The read-role request is rejected by the guard before RaitClaimContextService.read() runs. The test asserts the guard's 403 context {resource:'inf:rait-case',action:'claim-next',roles:['rait-coordinator']} (rait-claim-context.controller.ts @Resource/@Action). The service-level FORBIDDEN_ACTION carries no context. So this test would also pass at ca83c18d, where raitLockRiskRelations was the first statement. It was committed (36883cde) one minute before the fix (dd03c7ab), and no HTTP RED exists for it. Only the three-case unit spec (rait-claim-context.spec.ts) exercises the service ordering. It uses a mocked tx. The only F6 path that a real request can reach through the guard is an authenticated rait-analyst with an ineligible or foreign pool_id (404 before locks). That path has no real-PG sensor against a held ops.parameter writer. The other R17 HTTP control checks the opposite case: an eligible caller that waits and is then rechecked.
findings.recommendation: Under bounded Inspector authority, add one real-PG HTTP control. A guard-passing rait-analyst requests a foreign or ineligible pool_id while an owner transaction holds RowExclusiveLock on ops.parameter. Assert that the request gets 404 before the writer releases, that there is no Lock wait blocked by the writer pid, and that there are no effects. Record its RED against the pre-fix service bytes, for example from a disposable checkout of ca83c18d. Either relabel the existing read-role control as a guard-precedence control, or keep it as an extra control. Runtime unchanged.

findings.detail: The legacy-provenance vector named 'wrongactivepool' inserts its wrong-pool inf.rait_case_pool_scope binding with active=false. Lines 2716-2720 then assert that the only active binding is still the canonical pool. What the vector actually proves is rejection of a wrong pool combined with an inactive binding. It does not prove that the resolver rejects an active binding to the wrong pool. pr211-inspector-calibration.json coverageLimits states this openly, but the vector name and the census still count it as an active-wrong-pool control. That overstates the semantic coverage of the R17 legacy-specific denials.
findings.recommendation: Either rename the vector, for example to 'wrongpoolinactivebinding', and adjust the census label, or, if existing constraints allow it, add a separate active-wrong-pool vector under its own approved Inspector scope. Keep the existing 409 CLAIM_LEGACY_UNVERIFIED and no-effects assertions unchanged.

F6 runtime correction (rait-claim-context.service.ts:279-296) verified. The order is now: authenticate, rait-analyst check, nonlocking pools(), then 404 for a foreign or ineligible pool_id or 400 for queue_cursor without a selection, all before any global lock. Only a selected pool then takes raitLockRiskRelations, followed by a locked same-Tx pools(captured operation) canonical-equality recheck (404 on drift), the existing R10 candidates fence and the final finalScope equality fence. The unselected none/choice path does no risk reads and takes no global locks. The operation clock (auth.tenants FOR SHARE, not an ADR-0058 locked relation) is now captured before the lock wait instead of after it. I judged this not a regression, but under long lock waits the instant can predate the locked reads.

Provider batching (rait-risk.providers.ts:155-270, 285-297, 554-566) was assessed as equivalent at the source level. Timer predicates match the old per-code instance rules. Parameter selection still requires exactly one row per tier, so dropping the order-by has no effect. The alert prefetch on ceiling_on<=today is equivalent because line 531 enforces clock.ceiling_on===due. Incidents are still filtered per incident_ref. Every lock is still FOR SHARE and is now taken before child qualification. Scalar qualify('timer')/policy/movement calls and their receipt dependencies are unchanged. The diff matches the approved one-path runtime inventory, and the packet hashes match approved-runtime-extensions.json. F1/F2/F4/F5 stay as resolved at ca83c18d; the reviewed delta does not touch the qualifyPolicy, Calendar, sorted-versions or risk-GET ordering paths.
